objective: Describe the temporal random-key schedules encoded by registered Film Grunge and Film Damage CPU source equations, and identify update holds or skips under explicitly labeled sample schedules.

effects: ArtifactFilmGrungeEffect: compositionFrame enters frameSeed = uint32(seed * 1664525 + frame * 1013904223).
FilmDamageCPUImpl: frameKey = floor(evolution * 24); rng seed = uint32(seed) XOR uint32(frameKey * 0x9e3779b9).
scope.method: Static-source equation audit and integer schedule model. No effect is executed and no candidate image is compared.
excluded: std::mt19937 output sequence or random-distribution behavior
perceptual flicker, image difference, motion compensation, and scene motion
perceptual response of rendered frames to a keyframed Evolution slope
color, alpha, resolution, image quality, runtime, memory, and performance acceptance
changes to product implementation or default values

comparison.baseline: The seed key held at a sampled output frame; this is an arithmetic reference only, not an image baseline.
schedules: 120 sequential integer Composition frames for Film Grunge.
120 evolution samples at increments 1/24, 1/30, and 1/60, each starting at zero for Film Damage.
A 1/48 evolution increment to expose holds and a 1/12 increment to expose skipped integer keys relative to the source's 24-key-per-unit mapping.
comparison.ground_truth: None. Source expression is the sole authority for the modeled integer mapping; image behavior is outside this plan.

materials.kind: Source code only; no pixel materials.
materials.identity: SHA-256 hashes of exact source bytes recorded in the output report.

conditions.seed: 1977 for schedule examples; integer-key properties are also described algebraically.
conditions.time: Composition keyframe time is RationalTime(compositionFrame, frameRate). Evolution is an animatable Float value evaluated at that time; schedules state the assumed value slope in units per timeline second. Its value unit is not otherwise specified.
conditions.metrics: Adjacent identical-key pairs, changed-key pairs, unique 32-bit seed count, key delta distribution, and skipped integer keys.
conditions.display: No display output; this is a numeric source audit.

effect_correctness.method: Verify source markers and reproduce their integer casts, floor, multiply, XOR, and uint32 wrap semantics.
effect_correctness.acceptance_criteria: Exact agreement with source equations and deterministic report generation; no image-level claim.

image_quality_and_detail.reason: No image was rendered or compared.

temporal_stability.method: Measure seed-key holds, changes, and skips in declared sample schedules.
temporal_stability.acceptance_criteria: Report key scheduling only; no perceptual or output-stability verdict.
temporal_stability.unverified: Rendered frame differences, exact keyframed values in user projects, motion interaction, out-of-order seek/reverse, and perceptual response.

render_paths_and_resolution.reason: No renderer or resolution-dependent image output was exercised.

execution.thresholds: No perceptual threshold; all observations are descriptive arithmetic counts.
execution.reproducibility: Record source hashes, script hash, Python version, exact schedules, and report hash.

amendments.reason: The initial 1/48 schedule demonstrates holds but cannot skip integer keys; the plan text incorrectly said it exposed skips.
amendments.change: Keep 1/48 as a hold case and add 1/12 as a skip case. Rerun the complete arithmetic schedule report against this amended plan before drawing conclusions.
amendments.scope_effect: No output-image comparison or acceptance condition changed.

amendments.reason: Static call-path review found Film Damage Evolution is a Float effect property and ArtifactAbstractEffect marks Float properties animatable, evaluates keyframes at RationalTime(compositionFrame, frameRate), then calls setPropertyValue before rendering.
amendments.change: Clarify that Evolution is an arbitrary keyframed scalar, not inherently seconds or frames. Label the 1/24, 1/30, and 1/60 sample steps as a linear ramp of 1 value unit per timeline second at 24/30/60 fps; label 1/48 and 1/12 at 24fps as slopes .5 and 2 units per second. Rerun the full schedule report.
amendments.scope_effect: The arithmetic samples are unchanged; their timeline interpretation is now explicit. Rendered appearance remains unmeasured.
